Any Ubuntu series that ships an older ovsdbapp, or an OVN version without Address_Set support, cannot take this fix without also updating those packages.

This is an RFE (new feature) that adds OVN driver behavior, not a bug fix. It may not meet SRU criteria. The stable backports are only tagged 'Related-Bug', and the cherry-picks needed conflict resolution in the tests and release note. No regression-risk or upgrade analysis is given for existing deployments, such as how existing ACLs and Address_Sets are migrated or synced.

The upstream backports exist only for stable/2024.2 and stable/2024.1. There is no backport for other series, and the tempest-plugin test job was only merged on master. Test coverage on the stable branches is therefore unclear.

bugs.title: Unable to create instances after a new compute node is added due to Ceph key rotation

blockers.summary: The fix is two-part: the nova-compute patch makes the charm send its application name early, and a companion ceph-mon patch is also needed. The ceph-mon fix is only reported as deployed to squid/stable. The bug does not show it reaching the older ceph-mon tracks that yoga and zed clouds use, so the nova-compute backport alone may not resolve the race there.

An earlier nova-compute-only workaround, moving send_application_name() to the top of ceph_joined(), did not stop the race. This suggests the nova-compute change is not sufficient without the ceph-mon change. The bug does not show that the backports were verified against a ceph-mon that carries the fix.

blockers.summary: The upload to jammy-proposed was rejected from the queue as 'languishing for over a month', so the fix is not in -proposed and needs re-uploading.

The fix changes the meaning of rados_connect_timeout: 0 now means no timeout (wait forever) and <0 means use the Ceph default. The glance charm sets 0 and may have relied on the old default, so existing deployments may regress. This is not covered in 'Where problems could occur' and has not been addressed.

The Test Plan is confusing and self-contradictory. It describes ceph and swift backends and then disables 'cinder', and it has no clear before/after verification steps or expected results. The reviewer asked for it to be rewritten.
The Impact section is unclear about what is being fixed and why. The reviewer asked for it to be improved, and the bug description still has the old text.

The commit that actually fixes the behavior (c197bbdc) is only 'Related-Bug', and the original 'Closes-Bug' commit merely deprecated the option. The description of what is being SRUed (one patch or both) is unclear, and the second patch's release-note behavior change is not reflected in the SRU template.

There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

blockers.summary: The fix has not yet been confirmed as uploaded or fixed in the development series (tenacious). The version was rebased once, but the reviewer asked that the devel fix land first, and whershberger says he cannot upload to -devel and that the AppArmor team still needs to review and accept it. SRU releases are blocked until then.

The bug has no 'Target to series' tracking, and [ Impact ] does not say which Ubuntu releases are affected. The SRU team cannot tell which stable series need the patch, and the debdiffs and PPA appear to cover devel only, with no per-series SRU uploads.

The patch's DEP-3 header lacks an Author field (needed for Origin to be optional), and the extended description does not explain why the change is needed. It is not shown that these were fixed in the re-upload.

The test plan does not say how to set up the LVM test environment (LXD VM, multipass, etc.), and it edits the profile by hand with nano instead of installing the fixed package from -proposed (before/after the fix).
